problems.stem: You receive a sales export. Row 1 has the title 'Q3 Report', row 2 is blank, row 3 has the headers (Date, Region, Units), and the data starts in row 4. To build a clean tidy table that Excel features can use, what should you do first?
options: Leave it as is because the title looks professional at the top.
Delete rows 1 and 2 so the header row (Date, Region, Units) is row 1 with no blank rows above the data.
Merge cells A1:C1 so the title spans the table.
Color the header row so it stands out from the title.
problems.explanation: A tidy table needs one header row at the top with no title or blank rows above it, so Excel reads the column names correctly. The title belongs in a chart or a separate cell, not stacked above the data.

problems.stem: Column C holds dollar amounts. Some cells show 1250, others show '$1,250.00', and one shows '1250 USD'. A SUM over the column returns far less than expected. What is the most likely cause?
options: Excel cannot add more than 100 numbers at once.
The cells containing '$1,250.00' and '1250 USD' are stored as text, so SUM ignores them.
The SUM function only works on whole numbers.
The column is too narrow to hold the values.
problems.explanation: When numbers are entered with currency symbols or unit words inside the cell, Excel may store them as text. Text values are skipped by SUM. Store the raw number and apply currency formatting through cell format instead.

problems.stem: A roster has one column 'Name' with values like 'Lopez, Maria'. You need to sort by last name and also greet students by first name. What is the cleanest structural fix?
options: Re-type every name by hand in the order you prefer.
Split the one column into two columns, Last and First, using Text to Columns on the comma so each value lives in its own column.
Sort the column alphabetically and assume last name comes first.
Hide the Name column and add a note about the order.
problems.explanation: One value per cell is a core tidy-data rule. Text to Columns split on the comma gives a Last column and a First column, so each can be sorted or used independently.

problems.stem: Your Region column contains 'TX', 'Tx', 'texas', and 'Texas'. A pivot count treats these as four different regions. What is the right clean-up move before summarizing?
options: Accept the four labels because they all refer to Texas anyway.
Standardize the values to one consistent spelling and case (for example, all 'TX') so each region groups as one category.
Add a footnote explaining the four versions mean the same thing.
Sort the column so the versions sit next to each other.
problems.explanation: Inconsistent category labels split one real group into several. Standardizing spelling and case before any pivot or chart keeps the counts honest.
